Tune the Concert Hall

Fix the digital twin of a real concert hall in Milan, one line of code at a time.

● Easy⏱ 25 min🧩 3 levels + bonus👶 No coding experience needed
Room completed: 0%

Who are you?

You are the sound engineer of a concert hall in Milan. The hall has 800 seats. Your job: everybody in the hall must hear well.

What is a digital twin?

A digital twin is a copy of the hall that lives in the computer. It is more than a drawing:

  • it watches the real hall with sensors,
  • it thinks about what it sees,
  • and it can change things in the real hall, for example the loudspeakers.

Tonight the twin makes 3 mistakes. You will find them and fix them.

Look at the hall

This is the hall from above. The numbers show what is inside.

1Stage. The orchestra plays here, or a person gives a talk.
2Seats. Each dot is a seat. An orange dot means a person sits there.
3Microphones. There are 3. They hang from the ceiling and hear how loud the hall is.
4People counter. It is at the doors. It counts the people who come in and go out.
5Thermometer. It tells how warm the hall is.
6Back loudspeaker. It helps people at the back hear. The twin controls it.
7Sound preset. The sound setting of the hall: ORCHESTRA for music, SPEECH for a talk. It can be switched.

The sensors

A sensor is a small machine that measures something and tells the twin. Our hall in Milan has 3 kinds of sensors:

SensorIt tells the twin…How often
🎤 3 microphoneshow loud the hall is (in dB)every second
🚪 people counterhow many people are insideevery 5 seconds
🌡 thermometerhow warm it is (in °C)every 10 seconds

Some sensors are fast, some are slow. The twin always keeps the last number it got from the slow ones.
